blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how to work with temperatures below zero or money owed? These are examples of directed numbers!

blocks.markdown: Directed numbers are numbers that have both magnitude and direction. They can be positive or negative. Positive numbers are greater than zero, while negative numbers are less than zero.

blocks.title: Directed Numbers
blocks.text: Directed numbers include both positive and negative numbers, indicating values above or below a reference point, such as zero.

blocks.markdown: To visualize directed numbers, we often use a number line. On a number line, positive numbers are placed to the right of zero, and negative numbers are placed to the left.

blocks.title: Placing Numbers on a Number Line
blocks.prompt: Place the numbers -3, 0, and 4 on a number line.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal line and mark a point in the middle as 0.
Place the number 4 three units to the right of 0.
Place the number -3 three units to the left of 0.

blocks.answer: The numbers -3, 0, and 4 are placed on the number line with -3 on the left, 0 in the center, and 4 on the right.

blocks.markdown: When adding or subtracting directed numbers, consider the direction. Adding a positive number moves to the right, while adding a negative number moves to the left.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember: Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding its positive counterpart.

points: Directed numbers can be positive or negative and are used to represent values above or below a reference point.
Use a number line to visualize the addition and subtraction of directed numbers.
